summary: Single-exporter contract for the lifecycle engine

delivery.outcome: The lifecycle engine has one named exporter and the six vendored copies are declared facades bound to a parity gate, so drift cannot start silently
nonGoals: No code moved or deleted in any lifecycle repository
No parity workflow added to the six consumers in this ticket
No change to the engine itself

architecture.decision: wellmanifest/lifecycle owns the engine: it holds src/lifecycle.py plus tests/test_lifecycle.py and its README states the core is deliberately domain-independent. The six standard/lifecycle.py files in git-, legal-, product-, saas-, ticket- and twin-lifecycle are byte-identical vendored copies of it, so they are facades under the contractOwnership=single-exporter rule this repository already defines for commercial sheets. Record that contract here; the parity gate itself belongs to the consumers and is separate follow-up work. This ticket moves no responsibility: the engine already lives in wellmanifest/lifecycle and the six copies already exist. It records the ownership that is in place and names the missing gate.
architecture.rollback: Revert the README section; no consumer repository is touched

validation.evidence: README names wellmanifest/lifecycle as the exporter of the lifecycle engine and the six repositories as facades
Prints 1: the exporter and all six facades are still byte-identical, so the contract records the current state rather than proposing a migration
Gate resolves the diff to ticket-005
